annotationRationale: The method uses prime factorization and the prime factors required for divisibility. The prime 23 forces the minimum, while the factors 8, 11, and 23 establish sufficiency.
sourceMethod: Follows the official prime-factorization argument, making explicit why n below 23 fails and why 23! contains all required factors.

review.mathCheck: For \(n<23\), no factor in \(n!\) is divisible by the prime 23, so 2024 cannot divide it. At \(n=23\), the distinct terms 8, 11 and 23 multiply to 2024. Hence the least value is 23, choice D, matching the key.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Originally worded, faithful expansion of MAA Q4 on page 3. It uses the same prime factorization and explicitly proves both directions of the official divisibility threshold.
review.annotationCheck: The explanation establishes necessity and sufficiency without overlooking the required power of 2. The prime-factorization annotation matches the method; successive prime-power valuation counting is unnecessary.
